texts.facts: Petitioner has preferred this misc. petition seeking quashing of FIR No.568/2019 registered at Police Station Vishvkarma Industrial Area, Jaipur(West), for offences under Sections 420 and 120-B of IPC. 2.
texts.arguments: It is contended by counsel for the petitioner that petitioner is working as proprietor of M/s Krishna Marketing which is having registration of Postman, Sunrise Gold and Satvik Gold. It is also contended that petitioner himself has registration to market soyabean oil, so allegation in the FIR that the petitioner changed Mohan Jhalani S/O Shri Ram Pratap ... vs State Of Rajasthan on 18 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199179299/ 1 the wrapper of the product of some other manufacturer and in that place pasted his own wrappers is incorrect. It is also contended that no offence under Sections 420 and 120-B of IPC is made out as there is no evidence that the products have been sold (Downloaded on 25/02/2020 at 09:15:37 PM) (2 of 3) [CRLMP-22/2020] in the market. It is also contended that police has no authority to raid the premises of the petitioner. 3. Counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance upon "Malkiat Singh & Anr. Vs The State of Punjab, 1969(1) SCC 157" and also on the provisions under Sections 68, 70 and 73 of The Food Safety and Standards Act 2006. 4. Learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the misc. petition. It is contended that FIR prima facie discloses commission of cognizable offence. Petitioner was involved in changing the wrapper of soyabean oil manufactured by some other manufacturers and then pasted his own wrapper of groundnut oil, therefore, committing the offence of cheating. It is also contended that police has concluded the investigation and has come to the conclusion that offence is made out. Police has also collected the wrappers which were removed from the tins and have details of the places where the products were sold after pasting the wrappers of Postman and Sunrise Gold.
